push-ups.name: Push-Ups
cues: Hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to the floor, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle.
Press through your palms to return to the start.

incline-push-ups.name: Incline Push-Ups
cues: Place hands on a bench or elevated surface.
The higher the surface, the easier the exercise.
Maintain a straight body line.
Focus on full range of motion.

decline-push-ups.name: Decline Push-Ups
cues: Place feet on a bench or elevated surface.
This increases the load on your upper chest and shoulders.
Keep your core tight to prevent your back from sagging.
Control the movement throughout.

bodyweight-squats.name: Bodyweight Squats
cues: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Keep your chest up and core engaged.
Push your hips back and bend your knees as if sitting in a chair.
Go down until thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

box-squats.name: Box Squats
cues: Place a box or chair behind you.
Squat down until you gently touch the box.
Pause for a second, then stand back up.
This helps control depth and build confidence.

jump-squats.name: Jump Squats
cues: Perform a regular squat, then explode upward into a jump.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Immediately absorb the impact and go into the next rep.
Use your arms for momentum.

plank.name: Plank
cues: Position on forearms, elbows directly under shoulders.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and glutes to prevent hip sag.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

knee-plank.name: Knee Plank
cues: Perform the plank on your knees instead of your toes.
Keep a straight line from your head to your knees.
Focus on feeling the contraction in your abs.
Gradually increase hold time.

plank-arm-leg-lift.name: Plank with Arm/Leg Lift
cues: From a stable plank, slowly lift one arm or leg off the ground.
Hold for 2-3 seconds without letting your hips rotate.
Alternate limbs.
This challenges your core stability.

forward-lunges.name: Forward Lunges
cues: Step forward with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keep your front knee over your ankle, not past your toes.
Push off the front foot to return to the starting position.

static-split-squats.name: Static Split Squats
cues: Start in a staggered stance without the stepping motion.
Lower and raise your body, focusing on balance.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
Use a wall for support if needed.

walking-lunges.name: Walking Lunges
cues: Instead of pushing back, step forward with the back leg into the next lunge.
This creates a continuous walking motion.
Maintain an upright torso and engaged core.
Cover a set distance or number of steps.

glute-bridges.name: Glute Bridges
cues: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Lower your hips back down with control.

partial-glute-bridges.name: Partial Glute Bridges
cues: Lift your hips only halfway up.
Focus on initiating the movement by squeezing your glutes.
Hold the top position for a moment.
Gradually increase the range of motion.

single-leg-glute-bridge.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
cues: Extend one leg straight out.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot to lift your hips.
Keep your hips level throughout the movement.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

burpees.name: Burpees
cues: Start standing, then drop into a squat with hands on the floor.
Kick your feet back to a plank position.
Perform a push-up.
Jump your feet back to the squat position and jump up explosively.

no-push-up-burpee.name: No Push-Up Burpee
cues: Perform the burpee motion without the push-up.
You can also step your feet back and forward instead of jumping.
Focus on a steady pace.
This reduces the intensity and strength requirement.

burpee-tuck-jump.name: Burpee with Tuck Jump
cues: At the top of the burpee, instead of a standard jump, pull your knees to your chest.
This adds an explosive, athletic component.
Land softly and transition smoothly into the next rep.
Increases cardiovascular demand significantly.

mountain-climbers.name: Mountain Climbers
cues: Start in a high plank position.
Keep your back flat and abs engaged.
Drive one knee towards your chest, then quickly switch legs.
Maintain a running or climbing motion.

slow-mountain-climbers.name: Slow Mountain Climbers
cues: Perform the movement slowly and deliberately.
Pause for a second with each knee drive.
Focus on core stability and control.
This builds foundational strength.

cross-body-mountain-climbers.name: Cross-Body Mountain Climbers
cues: Drive your knee towards the opposite elbow.
This twisting motion engages your obliques more.
Keep your hips low and stable.
Adds a rotational challenge to the core.

hollow-body-hold.name: Hollow Body Hold
cues: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your legs and shoulders slightly off the ground.
Keep arms and legs extended, creating a 'banana' shape.
Hold the position, keeping your core tight.

tuck-hollow-hold.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
cues: Bend your knees and bring them towards your chest.
This shortens the lever, making it easier to hold.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Gradually extend your legs as you get stronger.

hollow-body-rocks.name: Hollow Body Rocks
cues: From the hollow hold, gently rock back and forth.
Maintain the hollow shape throughout the rock.
The movement should be small and controlled.
This adds a dynamic challenge to core stability.

superman.name: Superman
cues: Lie face down with arms and legs extended.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back.
Hold for a moment at the top, then lower with control.

alternating-superman.name: Alternating Superman
cues: Lift your right arm and left leg simultaneously.
Lower and then lift your left arm and right leg.
This reduces the load and helps with coordination.
Focus on slow, controlled movements.

superman-flutter-kicks.name: Superman Hold with Flutter Kicks
cues: Hold the top position of the superman.
Perform small, quick flutter kicks with your legs.
Keep your chest and arms lifted.
This increases time under tension and difficulty.

pistol-squat.name: Pistol Squat
cues: Balance on one leg, extending the other leg forward.
Lower yourself into a full squat on the standing leg.
Keep your heel on the ground and chest up.
Drive through your heel to return to the standing position.

box-pistol-squat.name: Box Pistol Squat
cues: Perform the movement while squatting down to a bench or box.
This limits the range of motion and provides a target.
Use a higher box to make it easier, lower for harder.
Focus on control and balance.

elevated-pistol-squat.name: Elevated Pistol Squat
cues: Stand on a box or bench.
This allows your non-working leg to drop lower.
It requires more strength as there's no 'bottoming out'.
Focus on a deep, controlled squat.

pull-ups.name: Pull-ups
cues: Grip the bar with palms facing away, slightly wider than shoulders.
Start from a dead hang with arms fully extended.
Pull your chest towards the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself with control until arms are straight again.

band-assisted-pull-ups.name: Band-Assisted Pull-ups
cues: Loop a resistance band around the bar and place your feet or knees in it.
The band provides assistance at the bottom of the movement.
Use a thicker band for more help, a thinner one for less.
Focus on the same pulling mechanics.

weighted-pull-ups.name: Weighted Pull-ups
cues: Add weight using a dip belt or by holding a dumbbell between your feet.
This overloads the muscles for strength and size.
Maintain strict form; don't sacrifice quality for weight.
Start with a light weight and increase gradually.

chin-ups.name: Chin-ups
cues: Grip the bar with palms facing you, shoulder-width apart.
Pull up until your chin is over the bar.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top.
Lower yourself fully with control.

negative-chin-ups.name: Negative Chin-ups
cues: Jump or use a box to get your chin over the bar.
Lower yourself as slowly as possible (aim for 3-5 seconds).
This builds the eccentric (lowering) strength.
Reset and repeat.

close-grip-chin-ups.name: Close-Grip Chin-ups
cues: Bring your hands closer together on the bar.
This increases the focus and demand on your biceps.
Pull your chest to the bar.
Keep the movement strict and controlled.

hanging-leg-raises.name: Hanging Leg Raises
cues: Hang from the bar with arms extended.
Keep your legs straight and together.
Raise your legs as high as you can without swinging.
Lower your legs slowly and with control.

hanging-knee-raises.name: Hanging Knee Raises
cues: Hang from the bar with arms extended.
Bend your knees and raise them towards your chest.
This shortens the lever, making it easier.
Focus on using your abs, not momentum.

toes-to-bar.name: Toes-to-Bar
cues: Initiate the movement by pulling down on the bar with your lats.
Use your abs to bring your toes up to touch the bar.
Requires a combination of strength and coordination.
Control the descent to avoid excessive swinging.

dumbbell-bicep-curls.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curls
cues: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Keep elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl weights up toward shoulders without swinging your body.
Squeeze biceps at the top and lower with control.

seated-bicep-curls.name: Seated Bicep Curls
cues: Sit on a bench or chair for stability.
This helps prevent using momentum from your lower body.
Focus on isolating the bicep muscle.
Use a lighter weight to perfect form.

incline-dumbbell-curls.name: Incline Dumbbell Curls
cues: Lie back on an incline bench (30-45 degrees).
This puts your biceps in a stretched position, increasing the difficulty.
Let your arms hang straight down before curling.
Keep your shoulders back and down.

bent-over-dumbbell-rows.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rows
cues: Hinge at your hips with a slight bend in your knees, back straight.
Pull dumbbells to your lower ribs, keeping elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Control the weight on the way down.

chest-supported-row.name: Chest-Supported Row
cues: Lie face down on an incline bench.
This supports your torso and isolates the back muscles.
Row the dumbbells up, squeezing your back.
Prevents cheating and protects the lower back.

renegade-rows.name: Renegade Rows
cues: Start in a plank position holding dumbbells.
Row one dumbbell up while maintaining a stable plank.
Keep your hips level and core extremely tight.
Alternate arms with each rep.

dumbbell-bench-press.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and back slightly arched.
Press the weights straight up over your chest.
Lower with control until the dumbbells are near your chest.

dumbbell-floor-press.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
cues: Lie on the floor instead of a bench.
This limits the range of motion, which can be safer for shoulders.
Press up from the floor, stopping when your elbows touch down.
Focus on a powerful press.

incline-dumbbell-press.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
This targets the upper portion of your chest.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly back.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability on the incline.

dumbbell-overhead-press.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
cues: Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Keep your core tight and back straight.
Press the dumbbells directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the weights back to your shoulders with control.

seated-overhead-press.name: Seated Overhead Press
cues: Sitting on a bench with back support provides more stability.
This allows you to focus purely on the pressing motion.
Prevents using leg drive to cheat the weight up.
Ideal for learning the movement pattern.

arnold-press.name: Arnold Press
cues: Start with palms facing you at shoulder height.
As you press up, rotate your palms to face forward at the top.
Reverse the motion on the way down.
This hits all three heads of the deltoid.

bulgarian-split-squats.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
cues: Place the top of your back foot on a bench behind you.
Hold dumbbells in each hand.
Lower your back knee towards the floor, keeping your front knee aligned with your foot.
Drive through your front heel to return to the start.

bodyweight-bulgarian-split-squats.name: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squats
cues: Perform the exercise without any dumbbells.
Focus on balance and achieving a full range of motion.
This is a challenging exercise even with just bodyweight.
Master the form before adding weight.

deficit-bulgarian-split-squats.name: Deficit Bulgarian Split Squats
cues: Elevate your front foot on a small platform (like a weight plate).
This increases the range of motion and the stretch on the glutes.
Requires excellent mobility and control.
Use lighter weight when first attempting.

kettlebell-swings.name: Kettlebell Swings
cues: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell in front.
Hinge at your hips to grab the kettlebell.
Hike the bell back between your legs, then explosively drive your hips forward.
Swing the kettlebell to chest height, letting your arms guide it.
This is a hip hinge, not a squat.

kettlebell-deadlifts.name: Kettlebell Deadlifts
cues: Practice the hip hinge movement without the explosive swing.
Stand over the kettlebell, hinge at the hips, and lift.
Focus on keeping your back flat and driving with your glutes.
This builds the foundational pattern for the swing.

single-arm-kettlebell-swings.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swings
cues: Perform the swing with one arm.
This requires more core strength to prevent your body from rotating.
Keep your non-working arm out for balance.
Switch arms halfway through the set or each set.

kettlebell-goblet-squats.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squats
cues: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at chest level.
Keep your elbows tucked in.
Squat down, keeping your chest up and back straight.
The weight in front helps you maintain an upright posture.
Drive through your heels to stand up.

double-kettlebell-front-squat.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
cues: Clean two kettlebells into the rack position.
This significantly increases the load and core demand.
Requires strong wrists and core to maintain the rack position.
Keep your elbows high and torso upright.

turkish-get-up.name: Turkish Get-Up
cues: A complex, multi-step movement from lying to standing.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell at all times.
Move slowly and deliberately through each step.
Focus on stability and control, not speed.

half-turkish-get-up.name: Half Turkish Get-Up
cues: Perform only the first few steps, up to the seated position.
This builds core and shoulder stability for the full movement.
Practice without weight first to learn the sequence.
Master this before attempting the full get-up.

bottoms-up-turkish-get-up.name: Bottoms-Up Turkish Get-Up
cues: Hold the kettlebell upside down (bottoms-up).
This requires immense grip strength and shoulder stability.
Use a very light weight.
Any deviation in form will cause you to lose control of the bell.

resistance-band-rows.name: Resistance Band Rows
cues: Anchor the band securely in front of you at chest height.
Pull the band toward your ribs, keeping elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the contraction.
Control the band as you return to the starting position.

lighter-resistance-band-rows.name: Lighter Resistance Band Rows
cues: Use a band with less tension.
This allows you to focus on form and the mind-muscle connection.
Complete the full range of motion with control.
Perfect the movement before increasing resistance.

single-arm-band-rows.name: Single-Arm Band Rows
cues: Perform the row with one arm at a time.
This challenges your core to resist rotation.
You can often achieve a greater range of motion.
Focus on squeezing the lat of the working side.

band-pull-aparts.name: Band Pull-Aparts
cues: Hold a light band with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms straight out in front of you.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return to the start with control. Don't let the band snap back.

wider-grip-band-pull-aparts.name: Wider Grip Band Pull-Aparts
cues: Place your hands further apart on the band.
This reduces the effective resistance.
Focus on initiating the movement from your back, not your arms.
Excellent for shoulder health and posture.

pause-band-pull-aparts.name: Pause Band Pull-Aparts
cues: Hold the fully contracted position for 2-3 seconds.
This increases time under tension for the target muscles.
Fight the urge to rush the reps.
Focus on a powerful squeeze in your upper back.

bench-dips.name: Bench Dips
cues: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside your hips.
Slide your hips forward off the bench, supporting your weight with your arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until they are at a 90-degree angle.
Press through your palms to return to the start.

bent-knee-bench-dips.name: Bent-Knee Bench Dips
cues: Keep your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
This reduces the amount of bodyweight you have to lift.
Focus on feeling the contraction in your triceps.
Keep your back close to the bench.

feet-elevated-bench-dips.name: Feet-Elevated Bench Dips
cues: Place your feet on another bench or elevated surface in front of you.
This increases the load on your triceps and shoulders.
You can add a weight plate to your lap for even more resistance.
Maintain control throughout the movement.

box-jumps.name: Box Jumps
cues: Stand in front of the bench or box.
Dip into a quarter squat and explode up, swinging your arms for momentum.
Land softly on the center of the box with your knees bent.
Step down, do not jump down.

step-ups.name: Step-Ups
cues: Place one foot fully on the bench.
Drive through the heel of the front foot to lift your body up.
Bring the other foot to meet it on the bench.
Step back down with the same trailing foot.

tuck-jump-box.name: Tuck Jump onto Box
cues: As you jump, pull your knees high towards your chest.
This requires more power and coordination.
Use a slightly lower box than your max height for safety.
Land in a deep squat position.

lower-step-ups.name: Lower Step-Ups
cues: Use a lower surface if a standard bench is too high.
This reduces the range of motion and strength required.
Focus on control and balance.
Gradually increase the height as you get stronger.

weighted-step-ups.name: Weighted Step-Ups
cues: Hold dumbbells in each hand to increase the load.
You can also add a high knee drive at the top for an extra challenge.
Keep your torso upright and core engaged.
This builds serious single-leg strength.

barbell-back-squat.name: Barbell Back Squat
cues: Position the bar on your upper back (traps), not your neck.
Keep your chest up and back straight.
Squat down by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

pause-squat.name: Pause Squat
cues: Pause at the bottom of the squat for 2-3 seconds.
Maintain tension and a tight core throughout the pause.
Explode up from the bottom position.
Builds strength out of the most difficult part of the lift.

barbell-bench-press.name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet firmly on the floor.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and down on the bench.
Lower the bar to your mid-chest, then press up powerfully.

close-grip-bench-press.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
cues: Take a shoulder-width grip on the bar.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body as you lower the bar.
This places more emphasis on the triceps.
Lower the bar to your lower chest.

barbell-deadlift.name: Barbell Deadlift
cues: Start with the bar over your midfoot, feet hip-width apart.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and hips down.
Drive the floor away with your legs to lift the bar.
Squeeze your glutes to lock out at the top. Don't hyperextend.

romanian-deadlift.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
cues: Start from the top position.
Hinge at your hips, keeping your legs almost straight (slight knee bend).
Lower the bar to just below your knees, feeling a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
This variation emphasizes the hamstrings and glutes.

barbell-overhead-press.name: Barbell Overhead Press
cues: Start with the bar in the front rack position on your shoulders.
Grip just outside your shoulders.
Keep your core and glutes tight to create a stable base.
Press the bar straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to clear the path.

push-press.name: Push Press
cues: Initiate the movement with a slight dip and drive from your legs.
This momentum helps you press heavier weight.
It turns the lift into a more full-body, explosive movement.
Catch the bar back on your shoulders on the way down.

barbell-bent-over-row.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull the bar to your lower chest / upper abdomen.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top and lower with control.

pendlay-row.name: Pendlay Row
cues: Start with the barbell on the floor for every rep.
Explosively pull the bar from a dead stop to your chest.
Return the bar to the floor under control.
This builds explosive power in the back.

landmine-press.name: Landmine Press
cues: Stand facing the landmine, holding the end of the barbell with both hands.
Press the bar up and forward in an arc.
Keep your core tight to prevent your back from arching.
Control the weight on the way down.

half-kneeling-landmine-press.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
cues: Kneel on one knee for a more stable base.
This reduces the demand on your core and improves stability.
Allows you to focus on the pressing motion with one arm.
Press with the arm on the same side as the down knee.

landmine-push-press.name: Landmine Push Press
cues: Add a dip and drive with your legs to initiate the press.
Use momentum from your lower body to help press the weight.
This allows you to lift heavier and is more athletic.
A more explosive, full-body movement.

landmine-row.name: Landmine Row
cues: Stand straddling the barbell and hinge at your hips.
Keep your back straight and nearly parallel to the floor.
Grip the bar with both hands (using a V-handle is common).
Pull the end of the bar to your chest, squeezing your back.

meadows-row.name: Meadows Row
cues: Stand perpendicular to the bar, using one arm.
This allows for a greater range of motion and a different angle of pull.
Use your non-working arm to brace against your knee.
Targets the upper back and lats effectively.

landmine-rotational-twist.name: Landmine Rotational Twist
cues: Stand facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar with both hands, arms extended.
Keeping your arms straight, rotate your torso to move the bar in an arc from one hip to the other.
Pivot on your feet as you twist.
Control the movement with your core.

bodyweight-torso-twists.name: Bodyweight Torso Twists
cues: Practice the rotational movement without weight.
Focus on feeling your obliques contract.
Keep your hips stable and rotate from your upper spine.
This builds the mind-muscle connection.

explosive-landmine-twists.name: Explosive Landmine Twists
cues: Increase the speed of the rotation while maintaining control.
This makes the exercise more powerful and athletic.
Focus on snapping the bar from side to side.
Ensure your core stays braced throughout.

parallette-dips.name: Parallette Dips
cues: Start in a support hold on the parallettes, arms straight.
Keep your chest up and shoulders down.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked in.
Go as deep as you comfortably can, then press back up.

foot-assisted-dips.name: Foot-Assisted Dips
cues: Keep your feet on the floor in front of you.
Use your legs to assist with the movement.
This reduces the amount of bodyweight you need to lift.
Focus on the upper body doing most of the work.

weighted-dips.name: Weighted Dips
cues: Use a dip belt to add weight or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
This overloads the muscles for greater strength gains.
Ensure you can do at least 10-12 bodyweight dips with good form first.
Maintain control and full range of motion.

parallette-l-sit.name: Parallette L-Sit
cues: Start in a support hold, arms locked out.
Lift your legs straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor.
Keep your toes pointed and legs together.
Depress your shoulders (push them down) and hold.

tuck-l-sit.name: Tuck L-Sit
cues: Instead of keeping legs straight, bend your knees and tuck them in.
This is a much easier position to hold.
Focus on keeping your hips high.
Gradually extend your legs as you get stronger.

v-sit.name: V-Sit
cues: From the L-Sit, continue to raise your legs higher.
Aim to get your torso and legs into a 'V' shape.
This requires significantly more core compression and strength.
Keep your arms locked and shoulders depressed.

parallette-push-ups.name: Parallette Push-Ups
cues: Grip the parallettes with a neutral grip, hands under your shoulders.
The parallettes allow for a deeper range of motion.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up to the starting position.

incline-parallette-push-ups.name: Incline Parallette Push-Ups
cues: Place the parallettes on an elevated surface like a bench.
This reduces the amount of bodyweight you are pushing.
Focus on getting a full range of motion.
A great way to build up to flat push-ups.

feet-elevated-parallette-push-ups.name: Feet-Elevated Parallette Push-Ups
cues: Place your feet on a bench or box.
This increases the load on your upper chest and shoulders.
The deficit from the parallettes makes this very challenging.
Keep your core tight to maintain a straight body line.

parallette-tuck-planche.name: Parallette Tuck Planche
cues: From a support hold, lean your shoulders forward past your hands.
Tuck your knees to your chest and lift your feet off the ground.
Keep your arms locked straight and protract your shoulder blades.
Aim to have your back parallel to the floor.

planche-leans.name: Planche Leans
cues: Start in a push-up position on the parallettes.
Lean your shoulders as far forward as you can, keeping arms straight.
Hold the lean for time to build shoulder strength.
This is the foundational strength builder for the planche.

advanced-tuck-planche.name: Advanced Tuck Planche
cues: From the tuck planche, open your hips to flatten your back.
Your back should be perfectly parallel to the ground.
This is a significant step up in difficulty.
Requires more forward lean and shoulder strength.

knee-push-ups.name: Knee Push-Ups
cues: Perform push-ups from your knees instead of your toes.
Keep a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
This reduces the amount of bodyweight you're pushing.

diamond-push-ups.name: Diamond Push-Ups
cues: Place your hands close together, forming a diamond shape with thumbs and index fingers.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower down.
This significantly increases tricep activation.
Maintain a straight body line throughout.

lunges.name: Forward Lunges
cues: Step forward with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keep your front knee over your ankle, not past your toes.
Push off the front foot to return to the starting position.

dumbbell-rows.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rows
cues: Hinge at your hips with a slight bend in your knees, back straight.
Pull dumbbells to your lower ribs, keeping elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Control the weight on the way down.

dumbbell-chest-press.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and back slightly arched.
Press the weights straight up over your chest.
Lower with control until the dumbbells are near your chest.

barbell-row.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull the bar to your lower chest / upper abdomen.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top and lower with control.

landmine-twist.name: Landmine Rotational Twist
cues: Stand facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar with both hands, arms extended.
Keeping your arms straight, rotate your torso to move the bar in an arc from one hip to the other.
Pivot on your feet as you twist.

exercise-ball-pull-in-2.name: Exercise Ball Pull-In
cues: Place an exercise ball nearby and lay on the floor in front of it with your hands on the floor shoulder width apart in a push-up position.

incline-cable-flye-2.name: Incline Cable Flye
cues: To get yourself into the starting position.
set the pulleys at the floor level (lowest level possible on the machine that is below your torso).

flexor-incline-dumbbell-curls-2.name: Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls
cues: Hold the dumbbell towards the side farther from you so that you have more weight on the side closest to you.
(This can be done for a good effect on all bicep dumbbell exercises).
Now do a normal incline dumbbell curl.
but keep your wrists as far back as possible so as to neutralize any stress that is placed on them.

clean-shrug-2.name: Clean Shrug
cues: Begin with a shoulder width.
double overhand or hook grip.
Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward.

car-drivers-2.name: Car Drivers
cues: While standing upright, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended straight out in front of you.
This will be your starting position.

alternating-hang-clean-2.name: Alternating Hang Clean
cues: Place two kettlebells between your feet.
To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

medicine-ball-chest-pass-2.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
cues: You will need a partner for this exercise.
Lacking one, this movement can be performed against a wall.

single-leg-push-off-2.name: Single Leg Push-off
cues: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on the box, heel close to the edge.

one-arm-kettlebell-push-press-2.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Push Press
cues: Hold a kettlebell by the handle.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward.
This will be your starting position.

smith-machine-overhead-shoulder-press-2.name: Smith Machine Overhead Shoulder Press
cues: To begin, place a flat bench (or preferably one with back support) underneath a smith machine.
Position the barbell at a height so that when seated on the flat bench.
the arms must be almost fully extended to reach the barbell.

decline-dumbbell-flyes-2.name: Decline Dumbbell Flyes
cues: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs.
The palms of your hand will be facing each other.

backward-drag-2.name: Backward Drag
cues: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.

dips-chest-version-2.name: Dips - Chest Version
cues: For this exercise you will need access to parallel bars.
To get yourself into the starting position.
hold your body at arms length (arms locked) above the bars.

chair-lower-back-stretch-2.name: Chair Lower Back Stretch
cues: Sit upright on a chair.

tricep-side-stretch-2.name: Tricep Side Stretch
cues: Bring right arm across your body and over your left shoulder.
holding your elbow with your left hand.
Then repeat for your other arm.

chin-up-2.name: Chin-Up
cues: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing your torso and a grip closer than the shoulder width.

lying-prone-quadriceps-2.name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
cues: Lay face down on the floor with your partner kneeling beside you.
Flex one knee and raise that leg off the ground, attempting to touch your glutes with your foot.
Your partner should hold the knee and ankle.
This will be your starting position.

seated-one-arm-dumbbell-palms-up-wrist-c.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
cues: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in your right hand.

alternating-renegade-row-2.name: Alternating Renegade Row
cues: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder width apart.
Position yourself on your toes and your hands as though you were doing a pushup.
with the body straight and extended.
Use the handles of the kettlebells to support your upper body.

recumbent-bike-2.name: Recumbent Bike
cues: To begin, seat yourself on the bike and adjust the seat to your height.

suspended-fallout-2.name: Suspended Fallout
cues: Adjust the straps so the handles are at an appropriate height, below waist level.

forward-drag-with-press-2.name: Forward Drag with Press
cues: Attach a dual handled chain or rope attachment to the sled.
You should be facing away from the sled, holding a handle in each hand.

seated-barbell-twist-2.name: Seated Barbell Twist
cues: Start out by sitting at the end of a flat bench with a barbell placed on top of your thighs.
Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other.

standing-calf-raises-2.name: Standing Calf Raises
cues: Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height.

barbell-side-split-squat-2.name: Barbell Side Split Squat
cues: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck).
Your feet should be placed wide apart with the foot of the lead leg angled out to the side.
This will be your starting position.

upward-stretch-2.name: Upward Stretch
cues: Extend both hands straight above your head, palms touching.

one-arm-side-deadlift-2.name: One-Arm Side Deadlift
cues: Stand to the side of a barbell next to its center.
Bend your knees and lower your body until you are able to reach the barbell.

v-bar-pullup-2.name: V-Bar Pullup
cues: Start by placing the middle of the V-bar in the middle of the pull-up bar (assuming that the pull-up station you are using does not have neutral grip handles).
The V-Bar handles will be facing down so that you can hang from the pull-up bar through the use of the handles.

cuban-press-2.name: Cuban Press
cues: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position.
Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor.
allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position.
This will be your starting position.

hyperextensions-back-extensions-2.name: Hyperextensions (Back Extensions)
cues: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench, tucking your ankles securely under the footpads.

round-the-world-shoulder-stretch-2.name: Round The World Shoulder Stretch
cues: Stand up straight with your legs together, holding a bodybar or broomstick.

reverse-plate-curls-2.name: Reverse Plate Curls
cues: Start by standing straight with a weighted plate held by both hands and arms fully extended.
Use a pronated grip (palms facing down) and make sure your fingers grab the rough side of the plate while your thumb grabs the smooth side.
Note: For the best results, grab the weighted plate at an 11:00 and 1:00 o'clock position.

split-jump-2.name: Split Jump
cues: Assume a lunge stance position with one foot forward with the knee bent.
and the rear knee nearly touching the ground.

double-kettlebell-push-press-2.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
cues: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders.

hang-snatch-below-knees-2.name: Hang Snatch - Below Knees
cues: Begin with a wide grip on the bar, with an overhand or hook grip.
The feet should be directly below the hips with the feet turned out.
Your knees should be slightly bent, and the torso inclined forward.
The spine should be fully extended and the head facing forward.

standing-overhead-barbell-triceps-extens.name: Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension
cues: To begin.
stand up holding a barbell or e-z bar using a pronated grip (palms facing forward) with your hands closer than shoulder width apart from each other.
Your feet should be about shoulder width apart.

t-bar-row-with-handle-2.name: T-Bar Row with Handle
cues: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving.
Load an appropriate weight onto your end.

barbell-incline-shoulder-raise-2.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
cues: Lie back on an Incline Bench.
Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width).
lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight.
This will be your starting position.

standing-long-jump-2.name: Standing Long Jump
cues: This drill is best done in sand or other soft landing surface.
Ensure that you are able to measure distance.
Stand in a partial squat stance with feet shoulder width apart.

suspended-row-2.name: Suspended Row
cues: Suspend your straps at around chest height.
Take a handle in each hand and lean back.
Keep your body erect and your head and chest up.
Your arms should be fully extended.

single-leg-stride-jump-2.name: Single-Leg Stride Jump
cues: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge.

reverse-flyes-2.name: Reverse Flyes
cues: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline.
Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

kettlebell-sumo-high-pull-2.name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
cues: Place a kettlebell on the ground between your feet.
Position your feet in a wide stance, and grasp the kettlebell with two hands.
Set your hips back as far as possible, with your knees bent.
Keep your chest and head up.

one-arm-lat-pulldown-2.name: One Arm Lat Pulldown
cues: Select an appropriate weight and adjust the knee pad to help keep you down.
Grasp the handle with a pronated grip.
This will be your starting position.

stomach-vacuum-2.name: Stomach Vacuum
cues: To begin, stand straight with your feet shoulder width apart from each other.
Place your hands on your hips.
This is the starting position.

hang-snatch-2.name: Hang Snatch
cues: Begin with a wide grip on the bar, with an overhand or hook grip.
The feet should be directly below the hips with the feet turned out.
Your knees should be slightly bent, and the torso inclined forward.
The spine should be fully extended and the head facing forward.

hamstring-smr-2.name: Hamstring-SMR
cues: In a seated position.
extend your legs over a foam roll so that it is position on the back of the upper legs.
Place your hands to the side or behind you to help support your weight.
This will be your starting position.

supine-chest-throw-2.name: Supine Chest Throw
cues: This drill is great for chest passes when you lack a partner or a wall of sufficient strength.
Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent.

clean-and-press-2.name: Clean and Press
cues: Assume a shoulder-width stance, with knees inside the arms.
Now while keeping the back flat.
bend at the knees and hips so that you can grab the bar with the arms fully extended and a pronated grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width.
Point the elbows out to sides.

straight-arm-dumbbell-pullover-2.name: Straight-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
cues: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

speed-squats-2.name: Speed Squats
cues: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes.
To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height.
Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded.
step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.

bench-sprint-2.name: Bench Sprint
cues: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on a bench or box with your heel close to the edge.

prone-manual-hamstring-2.name: Prone Manual Hamstring
cues: You will need a partner for this exercise.
Lay face down with your legs straight.
Your assistant will place their hand on your heel.

middle-back-stretch-2.name: Middle Back Stretch
cues: Stand so your feet are shoulder width apart and your hands are on your hips.

high-cable-curls-2.name: High Cable Curls
cues: Stand between a couple of high pulleys and grab a handle in each arm.
Position your upper arms in a way that they are parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing you.
This will be your starting position.

overhead-slam-2.name: Overhead Slam
cues: Hold a medine ball with both hands and stand with your feet at shoulder width.
This will be your starting position.

ab-crunch-machine-2.name: Ab Crunch Machine
cues: Select a light resistance and sit down on the ab machine placing your feet under the pads provided and grabbing the top handles.
Your arms should be bent at a 90 degree angle as you rest the triceps on the pads provided.
This will be your starting position.

barbell-incline-bench-press-medium-grip-.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
cues: Lie back on an incline bench.
Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms).
lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked.
This will be your starting position.

it-band-and-glute-stretch-2.name: IT Band and Glute Stretch
cues: Loop a belt.
rope.
This will be your starting position.

seated-one-arm-dumbbell-palms-down-wrist.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
cues: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in your right hand.

barbell-side-bend-2.name: Barbell Side Bend
cues: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck).
Your feet should be shoulder width apart.
This will be your starting position.

plyo-push-up-2.name: Plyo Push-up
cues: Move into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your hands and toes.

spider-curl-2.name: Spider Curl
cues: Start out by setting the bar on the part of the preacher bench that you would normally sit on.
Make sure to align the barbell properly so that it is balanced and will not fall off.

standing-low-pulley-one-arm-triceps-exte.name: Standing Low-Pulley One-Arm Triceps Extension
cues: Grab a single handle with your left arm next to the low pulley machine.
Turn away from the machine keeping the handle to the side of your body with your arm fully extended.
Now use both hands to elevate the single handle directly above the head with the palm facing forward.
Keep your upper arm completely vertical (perpendicular to the floor) and put your right hand on your left elbow to help keep it steady.

band-pull-apart-2.name: Band Pull Apart
cues: Begin with your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding the band with both hands.

goblet-squat-2.name: Goblet Squat
cues: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest.
This will be your starting position.

physioball-hip-bridge-2.name: Physioball Hip Bridge
cues: Lay on a ball so that your upper back is on the ball with your hips unsupported.
Both feet should be flat on the floor, hip width apart or wider.
This will be your starting position.

kneeling-arm-drill-2.name: Kneeling Arm Drill
cues: This drill helps increase arm efficiency during the run.
Begin kneeling, left foot in front, right knee down.
Apply pressure through the front heel to keep your glutes and hamstrings activated.

dip-machine-2.name: Dip Machine
cues: Sit securely in a dip machine, select the weight and firmly grasp the handles.

weighted-sissy-squat-2.name: Weighted Sissy Squat
cues: Standing upright.
with feet at shoulder width and toes raised.
This is your starting position.

speed-band-overhead-triceps-2.name: Speed Band Overhead Triceps
cues: For this exercise anchor a band to the ground.
We used an incline bench and anchored the band to the base, standing over the bench.
Alternatively, this could be performed standing on the band.

upper-back-stretch-2.name: Upper Back Stretch
cues: Clasp fingers together with your thumbs pointing down.
round your shoulders as you reach your hands forward.

sled-overhead-backward-walk-2.name: Sled Overhead Backward Walk
cues: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain.
Load the sled to a light weight.

on-your-back-quad-stretch-2.name: On-Your-Back Quad Stretch
cues: Lie on a flat bench or step, and hang one leg and arm over the side.

external-rotation-with-band-2.name: External Rotation with Band
cues: Choke the band around a post.
The band should be at the same height as your elbow.
Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.

car-deadlift-2.name: Car Deadlift
cues: This event apparatus typically has neutral grip handles.
however some have a straight bar that you can approach like a normal deadlift.
The apparatus can be loaded with a vehicle or other heavy objects such as tractor tires or kegs.

bent-press-2.name: Bent Press
cues: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
The wrist should rotate as you do so.
This will be your starting position.

seated-bent-over-one-arm-dumbbell-tricep.name: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
cues: Sit down at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in one arm using a neutral grip (palms of the hand facing you).

front-squats-with-two-kettlebells-2.name: Front Squats With Two Kettlebells
cues: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders.
Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders.
Rotate your wrists as you do so.

dumbbell-squat-to-a-bench-2.name: Dumbbell Squat To A Bench
cues: Stand up straight with a flat bench behind you while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

sandbag-load-2.name: Sandbag Load
cues: To load sandbags or other objects.
begin with the implements placed a distance from the loading platform.

reverse-band-bench-press-2.name: Reverse Band Bench Press
cues: Position a bench inside a power rack, with the bar set to the correct height.
Begin by anchoring bands either to band pegs or to the top of the rack.
Ensure that you will be position properly under the bands.
Attach the other end to the barbell.

one-arm-kettlebell-snatch-2.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Snatch
cues: Place a kettlebell between your feet.
Bend your knees and push your butt back to get in the proper starting position.

preacher-hammer-dumbbell-curl-2.name: Preacher Hammer Dumbbell Curl
cues: Place the upper part of both arms on top of the preacher bench as you hold a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

brachialis-smr-2.name: Brachialis-SMR
cues: Lie on your side, with your upper arm against the foam roller.
The upper arm should be more or less aligned with your body.
with the outside of the bicep pressed against the foam roller.

one-knee-to-chest-2.name: One Knee To Chest
cues: Start off by lying on the floor.

standing-cable-wood-chop-2.name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
cues: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and move the cable to the highest pulley position.

rack-delivery-2.name: Rack Delivery
cues: This drill teaches the delivery of the barbell to the rack position on the shoulders.
Begin holding a bar in the scarecrow position.
with the upper arms parallel to the floor.
Use a hook grip, with your fingers wrapped over your thumbs.

shoulder-stretch-2.name: Shoulder Stretch
cues: Reach your left arm across your body and hold it straight.

incline-push-up-close-grip-2.name: Incline Push-Up Close-Grip
cues: Stand facing a Smith machine bar or sturdy elevated platform at an appropriate height.

supine-two-arm-overhead-throw-2.name: Supine Two-Arm Overhead Throw
cues: Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent.

cross-body-crunch-2.name: Cross-Body Crunch
cues: Lie flat on your back and bend your knees about 60 degrees.

otis-up-2.name: Otis-Up
cues: Secure your feet and lay back on the floor.
Your knees should be bent.
Hold a weight with both hands to your chest.
This will be your starting position.

cable-one-arm-tricep-extension-2.name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
cues: With your right hand.
grasp a single handle attached to the high-cable pulley using a supinated (underhand.
You should be standing directly in front of the weight stack.

piriformis-smr-2.name: Piriformis-SMR
cues: Sit with your buttocks on top of a foam roll.
Bend your knees, and then cross one leg so that the ankle is over the knee.
This will be your starting position.

front-cable-raise-2.name: Front Cable Raise
cues: Select the weight on a low pulley machine and grasp the single hand cable attachment that is attached to the low pulley with your left hand.

kneehip-raise-on-parallel-bars-2.name: Knee/Hip Raise On Parallel Bars
cues: Position your body on the vertical leg raise bench so that your forearms are resting on the pads next to the torso and holding on to the handles.
Your arms will be bent at a 90 degree angle.

iron-crosses-stretch-2.name: Iron Crosses (stretch)
cues: Lie face down on the floor, with your arms extended out to your side, palms pressed to the floor.
This will be your starting position.

full-range-of-motion-lat-pulldown-2.name: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown
cues: Either standing or seated on a high bench.
grasp two stirrup cables that are attached to the high pulleys.
Grab with the opposing hand so your arms are crisscrossed about you and your palms are facing forward.

one-arm-high-pulley-cable-side-bends-2.name: One-Arm High-Pulley Cable Side Bends
cues: Connect a standard handle to a tower.
Move cable to highest pulley position.

smith-machine-leg-press-2.name: Smith Machine Leg Press
cues: Position a Smith machine bar a couple feet off of the ground.
Ensure that it is resting on the safeties.
After loading the bar to an appropriate weight, lie underneath the bar.
Place the middle of your feet on the bar, tucking your knees to your chest.

single-leg-lateral-hop-2.name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
cues: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle.
To get into the start position, stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent.

straight-arm-pulldown-2.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
cues: You will start by grabbing the wide bar from the top pulley of a pulldown machine and using a wider than shoulder-width pronated (palms down) grip.
Step backwards two feet or so.

kneeling-cable-crunch-with-alternating-o.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch With Alternating Oblique Twists
cues: Connect a rope attachment to a high pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.

pallof-press-2.name: Pallof Press
cues: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and—if possible—position the cable to shoulder height.
If not, a low pulley will suffice.

around-the-worlds-2.name: Around The Worlds
cues: Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling.
Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs.
To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent.
This will be your starting position.

palms-up-barbell-wrist-curl-over-a-bench.name: Palms-Up Barbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench
cues: Start out by placing a barbell on one side of a flat bench.

lateral-box-jump-2.name: Lateral Box Jump
cues: Assume a comfortable standing position, with a short box positioned next to you.
This will be your starting position.

triceps-overhead-extension-with-rope-2.name: Triceps Overhead Extension with Rope
cues: Attach a rope to a low pulley.
After selecting an appropriate weight, grasp the rope with both hands and face away from the cable.

knee-across-the-body-2.name: Knee Across The Body
cues: Lie down on the floor with your right leg straight.
Bend your left leg and lower it across your body.
holding the knee down toward the floor with your right hand.
(The knee doesn't need to touch the floor if you're tight.

stiff-legged-dumbbell-deadlift-2.name: Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift
cues: Grasp a couple of dumbbells holding them by your side at arm's length.

rope-crunch-2.name: Rope Crunch
cues: Kneel 1-2 feet in front of a cable system with a rope attached.

oblique-crunches-on-the-floor-2.name: Oblique Crunches - On The Floor
cues: Start out by lying on your right side with your legs lying on top of each other.
Make sure your knees are bent a little bit.

dumbbell-raise-2.name: Dumbbell Raise
cues: Grab a dumbbell in each arm and stand up straight with your arms extended by your sides with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight.
This will be your starting position.
Tip: The dumbbell should be next to your thighs with the palm of your hands facing back.

machine-preacher-curls-2.name: Machine Preacher Curls
cues: Sit down on the Preacher Curl Machine and select the weight.

kettlebell-pass-between-the-legs-2.name: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs
cues: Place one kettlebell between your legs and take a comfortable stance.
Bend over by pushing your butt out and keeping your back flat.

plate-pinch-2.name: Plate Pinch
cues: Grab two wide-rimmed plates and put them together with the smooth sides facing outward.

dumbbell-side-bend-2.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
cues: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist.
Your feet should be placed at shoulder width.
This will be your starting position.

side-leg-raises-2.name: Side Leg Raises
cues: Stand next to a chair, which you may hold onto as a support.
Stand on one leg.
This will be your starting position.

weighted-jump-squat-2.name: Weighted Jump Squat
cues: Position a lightly loaded barbell across the back of your shoulders.
You could also use a weighted vest, sandbag, or other type of resistance for this exercise.

one-arm-kettlebell-military-press-to-the.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Military Press To The Side
cues: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulder.
Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces inward.
This will be your starting position.

sled-push-2.name: Sled Push
cues: Load your pushing sled with the desired weight.

chest-stretch-on-stability-ball-2.name: Chest Stretch on Stability Ball
cues: Get on your hands and knees next to an exercise ball.

quick-leap-2.name: Quick Leap
cues: You will need a box for this exerise.

smith-machine-pistol-squat-2.name: Smith Machine Pistol Squat
cues: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height.
Step under it and position the bar across the back of your shoulders.

barbell-shoulder-press-2.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
cues: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack.
Position a barbell at a height that is just above your head.
Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward).

reverse-band-power-squat-2.name: Reverse Band Power Squat
cues: Begin in a power rack with the pins and bar set at the appropriate height.
After loading the bar, attach bands to the top of the rack, using either pegs or the frame itself.
Attach the other end of the bands to the bar.

lower-back-curl-2.name: Lower Back Curl
cues: Lie on your stomach with your arms out to your sides.
This will be your starting position.

frog-hops-2.name: Frog Hops
cues: Stand with your hands behind your head, and squat down keeping your torso upright and your head up.
This will be your starting position.

rope-straight-arm-pulldown-2.name: Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
cues: Attach a rope to a high pulley and make your weight selection.
Stand a couple feet back from the pulley with your feet staggered and take the rope with both hands.
Lean forward from the hip, keeping your back straight, with your arms extended up in front of you.
This will be your starting position.

squat-with-chains-2.name: Squat with Chains
cues: To set up the chains, begin by looping the leader chain over the sleeves of the bar.
The heavy chain should be attached using a snap hook.
Adjust the length of the lead chain so that a few links are still on the floor at the top of the movement.

keg-load-2.name: Keg Load
cues: To load kegs, place the desired number a distance from the loading platform, typically 30-50 feet.

reverse-machine-flyes-2.name: Reverse Machine Flyes
cues: Adjust the handles so that they are fully to the rear.
Make an appropriate weight selection and adjust the seat height so the handles are at shoulder level.
Grasp the handles with your hands facing inwards.
This will be your starting position.

double-kettlebell-snatch-2.name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
cues: Place two kettlebells behind your feet.
Bend your knees and sit back to pick up the kettlebells.

drag-curl-2.name: Drag Curl
cues: Grab a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward) and get your elbows close to your torso and back.
This will be your starting position.

thigh-adductor-2.name: Thigh Adductor
cues: To begin, sit down on the adductor machine and select a weight you are comfortable with.
When your legs are positioned properly on the leg pads of the machine, grip the handles on each side.
Your entire upper body (from the waist up) should be stationary.
This is the starting position.

cable-seated-lateral-raise-2.name: Cable Seated Lateral Raise
cues: Stand in the middle of two low pulleys that are opposite to each other and place a flat bench right behind you (in perpendicular fashion to you.
the narrow edge of the bench should be the one behind you).
Select the weight to be used on each pulley.

ez-bar-skullcrusher-2.name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
cues: Using a close grip, lift the EZ bar and hold it with your elbows in as you lie on the bench.
Your arms should be perpendicular to the floor.
This will be your starting position.

tuck-crunch-2.name: Tuck Crunch
cues: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor.
Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down.

one-arm-kettlebell-row-2.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Row
cues: Place a kettlebell in front of your feet.
Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position.
Grab the kettlebell and pull it to your stomach.
retracting your shoulder blade and flexing the elbow.

romanian-deadlift-from-deficit-2.name: Romanian Deadlift from Deficit
cues: Begin standing while holding a bar at arm's length in front of you.
You can stand on a raised platform to increase the range of motion.

barbell-shrug-behind-the-back-2.name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
cues: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands behind your back using a pronated grip (palms facing back).
Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart.
You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for better grip.
This will be your starting position.

single-leg-butt-kick-2.name: Single Leg Butt Kick
cues: Begin by standing on one leg, with the bent knee raised.
This will be your start position.

ball-leg-curl-2.name: Ball Leg Curl
cues: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.

standing-toe-touches-2.name: Standing Toe Touches
cues: Stand with some space in front and behind you.

muscle-snatch-2.name: Muscle Snatch
cues: Begin with a loaded barbell held at the mid thigh position with a wide grip.
The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed.
Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward.
The shoulders should be just in front of the bar.

incline-inner-biceps-curl-2.name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench.

triceps-stretch-2.name: Triceps Stretch
cues: Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.

log-lift-2.name: Log Lift
cues: Begin standing with the log in front of you.
Grasp the handles, and begin to clean the log.
As you are bent over to start the clean.
attempt to get the log as high as possible.

tricep-dumbbell-kickback-2.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
cues: Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso.
Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist.
Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor.
Make sure to keep your head up.

chest-push-from-3-point-stance-2.name: Chest Push from 3 point stance
cues: Begin in a three point stance, squatted down with your back flat and one hand on the ground.
Place the medicine ball directly in front of you.

one-leg-barbell-squat-2.name: One Leg Barbell Squat
cues: Start by standing about 2 to 3 feet in front of a flat bench with your back facing the bench.
Have a barbell in front of you on the floor.
Tip: Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other.

weighted-ball-side-bend-2.name: Weighted Ball Side Bend
cues: To begin.
lie down on an exercise ball with your left side of the torso (waist.

lying-glute-2.name: Lying Glute
cues: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.

sumo-deadlift-with-bands-2.name: Sumo Deadlift with Bands
cues: To deadlift with short bands.
simply loop them over the bar before you start.
Ensure that they under the back half of your foot, directly where you are driving into the floor.

janda-sit-up-2.name: Janda Sit-Up
cues: Position your body on the floor in the basic sit-up position.
knees to a ninety degree angle with feet flat on the floor and arms either crossed over your chest or to the sides.
This will be your starting position.

muscle-up-2.name: Muscle Up
cues: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings.
Initiate a pull up by pulling the elbows down to your side, flexing the elbows.

sumo-deadlift-with-chains-2.name: Sumo Deadlift with Chains
cues: You can attach the chains to the sleeves of the bar.
or just drape the middle over the bar so there is a greater weight increase as you lift.
Attempt to keep the ends of the chains away from the plates so you don't hit them when you lower the weight.

elliptical-trainer-2.name: Elliptical Trainer
cues: To begin, step onto the elliptical and select the desired option from the menu.
Most ellipticals have a manual setting, or you can select a program to run.
Typically.
you can enter your age and weight to estimate the amount of calories burned during exercise.

ankle-circles-2.name: Ankle Circles
cues: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.

leg-press-2.name: Leg Press
cues: Using a leg press machine.
sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.
(Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development.
however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

dumbbell-prone-incline-curl-2.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
cues: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline.
Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way).

barbell-ab-rollout-2.name: Barbell Ab Rollout
cues: For this exercise you will need to get into a pushup position.
but instead of having your hands of the floor.
This will be your starting position.

underhand-cable-pulldowns-2.name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
cues: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley.
Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height.
These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.

upright-row-with-bands-2.name: Upright Row - With Bands
cues: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length.
Grasp the handles using a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width.
The handles should be resting on top of your thighs.
Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight.

alternating-kettlebell-row-2.name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
cues: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet.
Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible.
As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.

one-arm-kettlebell-split-snatch-2.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Split Snatch
cues: Hold a kettlebell in one hand by the handle.

rope-jumping-2.name: Rope Jumping
cues: Hold an end of the rope in each hand.
Position the rope behind you on the ground.
Raise your arms up and turn the rope over your head bringing it down in front of you.
When it reaches the ground, jump over it.

seated-bent-over-rear-delt-raise-2.name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
cues: Place a couple of dumbbells looking forward in front of a flat bench.

one-handed-hang-2.name: One Handed Hang
cues: Grab onto a chinup bar with one hand, using a pronated grip.
Keep your feet on the floor or a step.
Allow the majority of your weight to hang from that hand, while keeping your feet on the ground.
Hold for 10-20 seconds and switch sides.

decline-smith-press-2.name: Decline Smith Press
cues: Place a decline bench underneath the Smith machine.
Now place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended.
Using a pronated grip that is wider than shoulder width.
unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms extended.

reverse-cable-curl-2.name: Reverse Cable Curl
cues: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley using a pronated (palms down) and shoulder width grip.
Make sure also that you keep the elbows close to the torso.
This will be your starting position.

drop-push-2.name: Drop Push
cues: Position low boxes or other platforms 2-3 feet apart.

cat-stretch-2.name: Cat Stretch
cues: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees.

smith-machine-close-grip-bench-press-2.name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
cues: Place a flat bench underneath the smith machine.
Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended.
Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the flat bench.
Using a close and pronated grip (palms facing forward) that is around shoulder width.

chair-leg-extended-stretch-2.name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
cues: Sit upright in a chair and grip the seat on the sides.

box-squat-2.name: Box Squat
cues: The box squat allows you to squat to desired depth and develop explosive strength in the squat movement.
Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you.
Typically.
you would aim for a box height that brings you to a parallel squat.

catch-and-overhead-throw-2.name: Catch and Overhead Throw
cues: Begin standing while facing a wall or a partner.

dumbbell-seated-one-leg-calf-raise-2.name: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise
cues: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench.

spider-crawl-2.name: Spider Crawl
cues: Begin in a prone position on the floor.
Support your weight on your hands and toes, with your feet together and your body straight.
Your arms should be bent to 90 degrees.
This will be your starting position.

chair-upper-body-stretch-2.name: Chair Upper Body Stretch
cues: Sit on the edge of a chair, gripping the back of it.

incline-barbell-triceps-extension-2.name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
cues: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms down) that is a little closer together than shoulder width.

olympic-squat-2.name: Olympic Squat
cues: Begin with a barbell supported on top of the traps.
The chest should be up, and the head facing forward.
Adopt a hip width stance with the feet turned out as needed.

board-press-2.name: Board Press
cues: Begin by lying on the bench, getting your head beyond the bar if possible.
One to five boards.
made out of 2x6's.

sledgehammer-swings-2.name: Sledgehammer Swings
cues: You will need a tire and a sledgehammer for this exercise.
Stand in front of the tire about two feet away from it with a staggered stance.
Grip the sledgehammer.

kneeling-high-pulley-row-2.name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
cues: Select the appropriate weight using a pulley that is above your head.
Attach a rope to the cable and kneel a couple of feet away.
holding the rope out in front of you with both arms extended.
This will be your starting position.

single-leg-glute-bridge-3.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
cues: Lay on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent.

latissimus-dorsi-smr-2.name: Latissimus Dorsi-SMR
cues: While lying on the floor.
place a foam roll under your back and to one side.
This will be your starting position.

power-partials-2.name: Power Partials
cues: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length.
The elbows should be close to the torso.

weighted-pull-ups-3.name: Weighted Pull Ups
cues: Attach a weight to a dip belt and secure it around your waist.
Grab the pull-up bar with the palms of your hands facing forward.
For a medium grip, your hands should be spaced at shoulder width.
Both arms should be extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip.

toe-touchers-2.name: Toe Touchers
cues: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor.
Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down.

push-up-to-side-plank-2.name: Push Up to Side Plank
cues: Get into pushup position on the toes with your hands just outside of shoulder width.

standing-dumbbell-triceps-extension-2.name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
cues: To begin, stand up with a dumbbell held by both hands.
Your feet should be about shoulder width apart from each other.
Slowly use both hands to grab the dumbbell and lift it over your head until both arms are fully extended.

elbows-back-2.name: Elbows Back
cues: Stand up straight.

clean-and-jerk-2.name: Clean and Jerk
cues: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand or hook grip just outside the legs.
Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels.
back straight.
This will be your starting position.

band-assisted-pull-up-2.name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
cues: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar.
You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.

seated-floor-hamstring-stretch-2.name: Seated Floor Hamstring Stretch
cues: Sit on a mat with your right leg extended in front of you and your left leg bent with your foot against your right inner thigh.

incline-cable-chest-press-2.name: Incline Cable Chest Press
cues: Adjust the weight to an appropriate amount and be seated, grasping the handles.
Your upper arms should be about 45 degrees to the body, with your head and chest up.
The elbows should be bent to about 90 degrees.
This will be your starting position.

alternate-leg-diagonal-bound-2.name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
cues: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.

monster-walk-2.name: Monster Walk
cues: Place a band around both ankles and another around both knees.
There should be enough tension that they are tight when your feet are shoulder width apart.

kettlebell-dead-clean-2.name: Kettlebell Dead Clean
cues: Place kettlebell between your feet.
To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

leverage-chest-press-2.name: Leverage Chest Press
cues: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height.
The handles should be near the bottom or middle of the pectorals at the beginning of the motion.

alternate-incline-dumbbell-curl-2.name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
cues: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length.
Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.
This will be your starting position.

front-dumbbell-raise-2.name: Front Dumbbell Raise
cues: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells on front of your thighs at arms length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs.
This will be your starting position.

atlas-stones-2.name: Atlas Stones
cues: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet.
Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone.
attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone.
Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.

bottoms-up-2.name: Bottoms Up
cues: Begin by lying on your back on the ground.
Your legs should be straight and your arms at your side.
This will be your starting position.

barbell-shrug-2.name: Barbell Shrug
cues: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands in front of you using a pronated grip (palms facing the thighs).
Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart.
You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip.
This will be your starting position.

upright-barbell-row-2.name: Upright Barbell Row
cues: Grasp a barbell with an overhand grip that is slightly less than shoulder width.
The bar should be resting on the top of your thighs with your arms extended and a slight bend in your elbows.
Your back should also be straight.
This will be your starting position.

wrist-roller-2.name: Wrist Roller
cues: To begin, stand straight up grabbing a wrist roller using a pronated grip (palms facing down).
Your feet should be shoulder width apart.

finger-curls-2.name: Finger Curls
cues: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing up; hands spaced about shoulder width.

calf-press-2.name: Calf Press
cues: Adjust the seat so that your legs are only slightly bent in the start position.
The balls of your feet should be firmly on the platform.

calf-press-on-the-leg-press-machine-2.name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
cues: Using a leg press machine.
sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.

shoulder-circles-2.name: Shoulder Circles
cues: With shoulders relaxed and arms resting loosely at your sides (or in your lap if you're seated).
gently roll your shoulders forward.

cable-shrugs-2.name: Cable Shrugs
cues: Grasp a cable bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a shoulder width or slightly wider overhand (palms facing down) grip.

upright-cable-row-2.name: Upright Cable Row
cues: Grasp a straight bar cable attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width.
The bar should be resting on top of your thighs.
Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight.
This will be your starting position.

russian-twist-2.name: Russian Twist
cues: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them.
Your legs should be bent at the knees.

sit-up-2.name: Sit-Up
cues: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them.
Your legs should be bent at the knees.

shoulder-press-with-bands-2.name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
cues: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length.
Grasp the handles and lift them so that the hands are at shoulder height at each side.

wide-grip-lat-pulldown-2.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
cues: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley.
Make sure that you adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height.
These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.

double-kettlebell-jerk-2.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
cues: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand.

standing-dumbbell-reverse-curl-2.name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Curl
cues: To begin, stand straight with a dumbbell in each hand using a pronated grip (palms facing down).
Your arms should be fully extended while your feet are shoulder width apart from each other.
This is the starting position.

two-arm-kettlebell-jerk-2.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Jerk
cues: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders.
Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you swing the kettlebells towards your shoulders.
Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward.
Squat down a few inches and reverse the motion rapidly driving both kettlebells overhead.

decline-ez-bar-triceps-extension-2.name: Decline EZ Bar Triceps Extension
cues: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.

smith-single-leg-split-squat-2.name: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat
cues: To begin, place a flat bench 2-3 feet behind the smith machine.
Then, set the bar on the height that best matches your height.
Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded.
step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.

lying-face-down-plate-neck-resistance-2.name: Lying Face Down Plate Neck Resistance
cues: Lie face down with your whole body straight on a flat bench while holding a weight plate behind your head.
Tip: You will need to position yourself so that your shoulders are slightly above the end of a flat bench in order for the upper chest.
neck and face to be off the bench.
This will be your starting position.

knee-circles-2.name: Knee Circles
cues: Stand with your legs together and hands by your waist.

glute-ham-raise-2.name: Glute Ham Raise
cues: Begin by adjusting the equipment to fit your body.
Place your feet against the footplate in between the rollers as you lie facedown.
Your knees should be just behind the pad.

rowing-stationary-2.name: Rowing, Stationary
cues: To begin, seat yourself on the rower.
Make sure that your heels are resting comfortably against the base of the foot pedals and that the straps are secured.
Select the program that you wish to use, if applicable.
Sit up straight and bend forward at the hips.

standing-hip-flexors-2.name: Standing Hip Flexors
cues: Stand up straight with the spine vertical, the left foot slightly in front of the right.

standing-barbell-calf-raise-2.name: Standing Barbell Calf Raise
cues: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes.
To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height.
Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded.
step under the bar and place the bar on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck).

kettlebell-one-legged-deadlift-2.name: Kettlebell One-Legged Deadlift
cues: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand.
Stand on one leg, on the same side that you hold the kettlebell.

alternating-cable-shoulder-press-2.name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
cues: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.

kettlebell-windmill-2.name: Kettlebell Windmill
cues: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot and clean and press it overhead with your opposite arm.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders.
Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward.
Press it overhead by extending the elbow.

rack-pulls-2.name: Rack Pulls
